acceptance: From another host, identify which phase holds the staging lease and for how long. A stalled stage must eventually yield the global lease without skipping fast checks or ownership validation. Add deterministic coverage with two queues, including preservation or recovery of the interrupted worktree and protection from a stale holder pushing.
body: Beryl incident by-o0gz: Jarvis PID 79360 renewed the global staging lease for over 11 minutes while staging stayed at 581b46dd and another host waited. The remote lease serialized working pushers but only exposed the owner and last renewal, so the justiciar could not tell whether the holder was executing a fast check, waiting for the ownership lock, or syncing Beads. The local push resumed after the exact Jarvis lease was removed. See scripts/enact.py (StagingLease, land, ownership_lock, sync_beads) and the two-host queue coverage in tests/test_integration.py.

title: Fix slow CI failure on macos

acceptance: Preserve useful, credential-safe Dolt push failure diagnostics in the final error. Retry the observed Windows sharing violation with bounded backoff on the relevant Beads and Dolt calls. Cover both cases with focused tests.
body: In Beryl incident by-h1uj, enact worktree create by-ix1t.10 created the Windows worktree but reported only generic rejections for all eight metadata push attempts. A subsequent enact claim also failed on bd show with Windows error "A file cannot be opened because the share access flags are incompatible." A serialized native Dolt push and a retried claim then succeeded. The first push failures could not be classified because sync_beads does not retain the push stderr.

comments.text: Beryl incident by-fjrj reproduced the Windows sharing violation after a slow CI failure, when report_ci_failure called bd list. A one-off retry limited to the database-open error was used to replay the report. Follow-up en-kmv covers durable failure reporting across a longer outage.

body:
Add a new Enact role, the Archivist, to this repository (Enact itself).

User's request (verbatim): "New enact role: the Archivist is a session that runs at the end of projects and cleans up technical documentation. It deletes the plan markdown file and makes edits to persistent project documentation and project-level agent skills describing the shipped state. This should be *minimal*, the documentation philosophy is "YAGNI". General pattern if there's no pre-established doc architecture: put technical content into a local agent skill which describes the project architecture (must work on both claude and codex), keep this as a single SKILL.md for small projects and allow companion references for large projects. Try to keep the total number of enact-owned markdown files in the repository <=5, even for a very large project."

Decisions/defaults (vizier, recorded without user input):
- Label `role:archivist`, emoji 📜. Spawned like other bead roles.
- The vizier files exactly one Archivist bead per plan-document run (and per large task prompt that is treated as a plan), as the last bead: it depends on all other top-level work in the run (final milestone and any final Mason/Sage gate), so it runs once the shipped state is final. Small task-prompt runs do not get one. AGENTS.md / invocation role restrictions apply to it like any other role.
- The Archivist deletes the run's plan document only if it is tracked in the project repository; never touches files outside the repo. It also removes plan links that would dangle.
- It describes the shipped state only (no history, no changelog, no future plans), edits minimally (YAGNI), and follows any pre-established doc architecture in the project. Absent one: one project-local agent skill describing the architecture, a single SKILL.md for small projects, companion reference files only for large ones; total Enact-owned markdown files in the repo <= 5 even for very large projects.
- The project skill must be discoverable by both Claude Code and Codex without duplicated content. Verify where each looks for project-level skills (e.g. `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` vs `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and pick a layout that works on macOS, Linux and Windows (beware git symlinks on Windows; a short AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pointer may be an acceptable fallback). Record the choice in `docs/design.md`.
- The Archivist delivers its edits like an executor (enact worktree, commit, `enact push`), then closes its bead.

Files to touch (at least): new `skills/enact/roles/archivist.md` (~100 lines, 80-column markdown, modeled on `mason.md`/`executor.md` and `common.md`); `scripts/enact.py` (`EMOJI`, `SPAWNED_ROLES`, the role list in `spawn_prompt` and the justiciar prompt text); `skills/enact/SKILL.md` (Roles section and Build the graph: when/how to file the Archivist bead, its dependencies); `README.md` role table and run description; `templates/AGENTS.md` roles-in-use line; `docs/design.md`; unit tests in `tests/test_unit.py` for the new role wiring. Keep changes backward compatible (live sessions use this repo directly). Deliver via `enact worktree create` / commit / `enact push`, never directly to master.

Run: task prompt, parallelism 1, all roles allowed. Acceptance (whole run): Archivist role exists, is wired into the helper and vizier skill, documented, fast checks pass, change reaches staging via enact push.

Warden review of 8542e39 (pushed fix in a6d6f57).
Found: (1) Ordering bug. The vizier wired the Archivist last with dependency edges (and, with milestones, a final docs epic because tasks cannot depend on epics). Follow-up beads filed mid-run under the run epic (common.md says to use the top epic) were not covered, so the Archivist could start before them and document a non-final state. (2) test_spawn_prompt_names_role_files asserted that every EMOJI key appears in the prompt, but ROLE_NOTICE is derived from EMOJI, so that check could never fail. The archivist spawn test only covered one role and asserted the exact title string.
Changed: enact next (schedule) now holds a role:archivist bead until it is the last open non-epic bead in the epic's scope. SKILL.md drops the final docs epic: the Archivist is a plain child of the run epic with no deps. I updated design.md and archivist.md to match. archivist.md also now says that a skill created by an earlier Archivist counts toward the 5-file budget; the old wording could read as exempting it on later runs. Replaced the two tests with one that checks every SPAWNED_ROLES label spawns with its own role file. Added integration test test_archivist_waits_until_it_is_the_last_open_work; it fails without the gate and passes with it. Moved the stray unittest.main() block in test_unit.py to the end of the file.
Left alone: the .agents/skills content + .claude/skills stub layout (sound; no symlinks, Windows-safe), the YAGNI and plan-retirement rules, README table rows over 80 columns (existing tables already exceed it). Graphs filed with the old explicit deps still work, because the gate only adds a condition. Fast checks pass; archivist and vizier integration tests pass locally.

Follow-up beads that sessions file later directly under the run's top epic (common.md 'Follow-up beads', Mason's lower-value ideas, the Archivist's own follow-ups) do not block it, so the Archivist can run while code changes are still landing and document a state that is about to change. Options: have enact next hold role:archivist beads until every other open descendant of the epic is closed, or have sessions that file run-level follow-ups add a dep edge to the Archivist. Prefer the helper rule if it stays small.

body: Warden en-b2c.1.10 reproduced a crash-recovery gap after 8bfcfff with real git and the actual enact ci CLI. Start a slow check that records its PID and cwd and waits on an external release file; kill only the coordinator after the check starts; start a replacement coordinator. The old check remains alive while the replacement removes and recreates the same ci-<tip> worktree and starts a second check there. Observed coordinator 27989 killed, old check 28024 still alive, replacement 28025 launched check 28062, both checks recorded the identical worktree. The OS guard correctly releases on coordinator death, but ownership does not cover the protected subprocess lifetime. Fix crash recovery so surviving checks cannot overlap or have their worktree removed; handle startup handoff without introducing an unprotected interval, preserve portable stdlib-only Python 3.11+ behavior and legacy compatibility, and document the lifecycle decision. This requires a coherent subprocess lifetime/ownership design beyond the PID-file publication patch; complete it within en-b2c and deliver through Enact. Keep a deterministic real CLI regression in normal CI.

body:
Final Mason audit found that cmd_lock uses exists/stat/write_text for acquisition and unconditional unlink for release. It records a session but never checks it. Reproduced against staging a394b33 with the public parser and a real temporary lock file: old-sweep acquire; new-sweep acquire --stale-minutes 0; old-sweep release; third-sweep acquire. All four operations succeed, so the old sweep removes its successor's lease. Concurrent initial acquires also have a check/write window. Marshal recovery attempts have their own durable bounds, but sweep cleanup and native actions rely on this advertised exclusion.

Replace the ad hoc file state with one small session-owned lease protocol: atomic acquisition and serialized expiry replacement/release, rejecting a release by a different owner. Prefer reusing the existing short-lived OS-lock primitive for lease mutations rather than inventing another lock framework; the command cannot hold an OS lock across separate chat tool calls. Preserve supported stale recovery and existing CLI shape where possible, and state the stale-expiry behavior explicitly. Do not change CI lock ownership semantics. Keep helper stdlib-only/Python 3.11+/portable, and record the decision in docs/design.md.

This is an essential follow-up in run en-b2c, parent gate en-b2c.2. All run restrictions and the existing Warden policy apply. Deliver through Enact worktree/commit/push only. No unrelated cleanup.

acceptance: Regression tests cover repeated Dolt push failures within the ownership lock and Windows share-access contention. A failed or timed-out sync releases the lock, preserves local writes for retry, and surfaces the Dolt error. No parallel embedded-store writes are introduced.
body: On Cygnus a vizier metadata update for Beryl by-ix1t.3 held the ownership lock long enough for enact start to time out at 180 s. The metadata command reported four rejected Dolt pushes before succeeding. A concurrent raw bd create also reproduced Windows incompatible share access while a Dolt command had the embedded store open. Inspect sync_beads, ownership_lock, and Beads.raw in scripts/enact.py. Distinguish transient rejections from non-retryable failures and preserve the underlying error. Ensure a worker can retry a busy start without losing its reservation and that helper-owned Beads reads tolerate brief Windows store contention.

comments.author: Derek Thurn
comments.text: Recurrence on Cygnus on 2026-11-14 (Beryl incident by-cyeb): the by-ix1t.4 executor's enact brief failed on both bd show and bd list with incompatible Windows share access. A concurrent raw bd create reproduced the error while enact next was in a Dolt SQL probe. Running the same show/create under Enact's existing ownership lock succeeded, and the executor had claimed its reservation and created its worktree. The vizier had repeatedly retried Dolt pushes. A direct push earlier in the same run exposed a non-fast-forward rejection. Include enact brief or an equivalent unlocked multi-read entry point in the regression coverage.

comments.author: Derek Thurn
comments.text: Beryl incident by-fjrj also reproduced this: the recovery reporter held the ownership lock across a scan of 1,326 delivered commits and several rejected Dolt pushes. The first scratch worktree create waited 180 s and timed out; a second attempt timed out while the next vizier command held the lock. The recovered Steward by-z3kx did eventually sync. Keep expensive ancestry scans outside long ownership lock intervals or batch the ancestry queries.

title: Bound Dolt sync lock holds and retry Windows Beads reads

acceptance: Validate the actual local worker launch path before reserving any bead. A disposable worker must report its effective policy and demonstrate the Git metadata and remote access Enact needs without a prompt. Stop preflight with the specific failed check if the app cannot support that launch path. Preserve the existing Claude path.
body: Beryl run by-7pm stalled because both local Codex worker chats launched with approval_policy=on-request and sandbox_policy=workspace-write, although the vizier had never and danger-full-access. Enact preflight verified only the vizier. The chat creation tool has no permission-mode parameter. Incident record: Beryl by-c3ja. Update skills/enact-plan/SKILL.md and the Codex desktop recovery workflow in docs/design.md using current app behavior.

body: Beryl incident by-fjrj: Cygnus reproduced a slow CI failure at 53ae3d11 and bisected it, but a transient Windows embedded Dolt sharing violation in report_ci_failure prevented ci_check_worker from updating ci-result.json and ci-last. The next CI wait still had no Steward and could trigger another full run. Keep the failed SHA, green base, and log excerpt durable before the first Beads call. Resume the reporting step when CI restarts, preserving the existing rules for superseded failures and associating the report with affected runs.

acceptance: Preserve pending local commits and ownership fencing across retries. Bound the time other local ownership operations wait during sustained remote contention. Log the concrete rejected-push diagnostic and add a deterministic contention regression test.
body: Beryl incident by-3lk5c: enact start by-q44s.7.7 held the Mac ownership lock for 296 s. The vizier timed out after 180 s. A fresh sync reproduced Dolt's main -> main (non-fast-forward) after the remote advanced. sync_beads logs only a generic rejection and holds the ownership lock through pulls, pushes, and backoff. See scripts/enact.py (sync_beads, ownership_lock, cmd_start) and the contention fixtures in tests/.
title: Bound Beads push retries under the ownership lock
